turns.doctor_question: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Nice to meet you, Dr. Smith. I came in because... well, I honestly just can't see my carpentry studio, or my life for that matter, getting back on track anymore. It just feels like no matter how hard I work, or... or what kind of payment plan they put in front of me, it's not going to make a difference. I'm just at a dead end with it all.

symptom_reasoning.S083: The patient expresses a profound sense of despair, stating they cannot see their life getting back on track and feeling they are at a dead end where nothing will make a difference.

turns.doctor_question: Have you ever experienced a period like this in the past where you felt this low or hopeless for weeks at a time?
turns.patient_response: I'm not really sure. I mean... I don't remember a specific time in the past where I felt exactly like this for weeks at a time. I've had rough patches, sure, but... nothing really comes to mind that was quite like what I'm dealing with right now.

turns.doctor_question: Was there a specific event or change in your life that happened shortly before you started feeling this way?
turns.patient_response: Yeah... it was when I took on the mortgage for the studio. That was a little over two years ago. I guess it's been about two years and two months now. That's when this all really started.

symptom_reasoning.S081: The patient confirms that their symptoms started in response to a specific identifiable stressor, which was taking on the mortgage for the studio.

turns.doctor_question: Have you felt this way every single day for the past two years, or have there been periods where you felt like yourself again?
turns.patient_response: I don't think I've had any time where I felt like my old self, no. It's... it's pretty much been every single day. I mean, maybe some days I'm just working and not thinking about it quite as much, but... the feeling is always there. I haven't really had a break from it since I signed those papers.

turns.doctor_question: Over these past two years, have you noticed any consistent changes in your appetite or your ability to sleep?
turns.patient_response: Not really, no. I mean... I still eat about the same as I always have. And my sleep... I guess my sleep hasn't really changed much either. I haven't noticed any real differences with either of those, honestly.

symptom_reasoning.S026: The patient explicitly states they eat about the same as they always have, denying any changes in appetite.
symptom_reasoning.S027: The patient explicitly states their sleep hasn't really changed much, denying any sleep disturbances.

turns.doctor_question: Over these past two years, have you felt a persistent sense of inadequacy or low self-esteem?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I'd say so. It's... it hits me hardest when I'm working. Like, if a joint doesn't line up perfect, or if I end up missing a bid deadline for a job, I don't just think, you know, "Oh, I made a mistake." I start thinking I'm just a lousy carpenter. I start telling myself that maybe I had no business trying to run my own studio in the first place. It just feels like I'm not good enough to be doing this.

symptom_reasoning.S042: The patient confirms feeling a persistent sense of inadequacy, stating they feel like a 'lousy carpenter' and 'not good enough' when they make mistakes.

turns.doctor_question: During these past two years, have you found that you still get enjoyment or pleasure out of the things you used to love doing?
turns.patient_response: Honestly, I still enjoy the things I used to. I mean... I still like watching football on the weekends, or just having a beer on the porch. That hasn't really changed. I haven't lost interest in that stuff, it's just... I guess I just feel weighed down while I'm doing them. But the enjoyment is still there.

symptom_reasoning.S025: The patient explicitly states they still enjoy the things they used to and have not lost interest in them.
